maya: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selector change, we see prefix cache hit-rate drop ~18% on small-seq workloads.
jorge: Observed on canary. Profiling shows KV lookup latency up and many partial matches falling through.
sophia: Do we have an A/B that isolates kernel path? Or is this confounded by batching change?
maya: It looks correlated: new kernel switches to packed-attention chunking and changed token alignment -> cache key canonicalization mismatch.
lee: If keying includes sequence-length or token offsets, that would invalidate keys. What's current key schema?
maya: Current key = model + quant + prefix_hash + start_token_index (was introduced for stream-resume). Suspect start_token_index causing divergence.
sophia: Ack. Streaming resumes / partial retries could be writing keys with different offsets. That's dangerous.
jorge: Suggested fix: canonicalize cache key by normalized prefix text + tokenizer-insensitive hash. Remove start_token_index except for explicit resume flows.
maya: Risk: removes resume optimization. Propose opt-in header so clients can choose strict keying vs resume-friendly keying: `x-redwood-cache-mode: strict|resume`.
lee: Example request header to opt into resume-friendly caching:
```http
POST /v1/generate
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <token>
x-redwood-cache-mode: resume
x-redwood-cache-optin: 1
```
sophia: Also need server-side dedupe to prevent retry storms from double-warming the cache. Retries with aggressive backoff are causing multiple fills.
maya: Maybe use a Warmup-ID and ignore duplicate fills within 10s per prefix-hash, or a short soft-lock on writes.
opsbot: canary-deploy-bot: rolling canary started for kernel-selector v2 on cluster-canary-3.
jorge: Telemetry request: add metric `cache.fill_from_client_retries` and tag with `retry_count` and `streaming=true/false`. We should graph this alongside hit-rate.
sophia: Also run a batch-size sweep. The packing kernel changed batching heuristics which is shifting average sequence length -> fewer cacheable prefixes end up in same batch.
maya: Action items: 1) rollback kernel change on canary if we can reproduce quickly; 2) add opt-in header + telemetry; 3) implement debounce/soft-lock on warmup writes; 4) run 48-72h canary with synthetic streaming/resume workload. I can own 1+2.
lee: ETA for header + telemetry patch?
maya: 48h for header + telemetry, 72h for debounce. Can start tests tomorrow morning.
sophia: OK. Ping me if `cache.fill_from_client_retries` > 0.5% per minute or if hit-rate delta > 10% in any region.
jorge: Quick SDK note: SDKs should expose a `cacheMode` option and default to `strict` for non-streaming helpers and `resume` for streaming helpers. Devex to PR.
maya: Thanks all. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: incident-tracker created INC-2026-0427 for regression tracking.
